rules.title: No rel=canonical on indexable page
rules.description: The page has no rel=canonical. Search engines pick a canonical themselves; explicit canonicals help consolidate duplicates (parameters, tracking, http/https, www).
rules.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="https://absolute-url"> pointing to the preferred URL (self-referential on unique pages).

rules.title: Multiple rel=canonical declarations
rules.description: More than one rel=canonical is declared. Google may ignore all of them when they conflict.
rules.fix: Keep exactly one rel=canonical (check templates, SEO plugins and JS that inject a second one).

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: Relative canonical URL
rules.description: rel=canonical uses a relative URL. Google supports it but recommends absolute URLs to avoid errors.

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: Canonical points to a non-200 URL
rules.description: The canonical target redirects or returns an error. Canonicals should point to a live, indexable 200 URL.
rules.fix: Point the canonical to the final 200 URL.
rules.verify: Fetch the canonical target and confirm 200.

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: Canonical points to a noindex page
rules.description: The canonical target carries noindex — conflicting signals (consolidate here, but do not index).
rules.fix: Point the canonical to an indexable page or remove noindex from the target.

rules.title: Canonical points to another domain
rules.description: Cross-domain canonicals are supported (e.g. syndicated content) but transfer consolidation away from this site. Listed for review.
rules.fix: Confirm the cross-domain canonical is intentional.

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: noindex used together with a canonical to another URL
rules.description: The page has noindex and a canonical pointing elsewhere. Google does not recommend noindex for canonicalisation.
rules.fix: Use rel=canonical (or a redirect) alone for duplicates.

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: Duplicate titles across pages
rules.description: Several indexable pages share the same <title>. Google recommends unique, descriptive titles per page.
rules.fix: Write a distinct title for each page that reflects its specific content.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and confirm titles are unique.

rules.title: Duplicate meta descriptions across pages
rules.description: Several indexable pages share the same meta description. Google recommends unique descriptions per page.
rules.fix: Write distinct descriptions summarising each page, or omit it where it cannot be unique.

rules.title: Duplicate page content without canonical consolidation
rules.description: Multiple URLs serve identical main text and do not canonicalise to a single URL. Search engines must choose a canonical themselves, splitting signals.
rules.fix: Redirect duplicates or add rel=canonical to the preferred URL.
rules.verify: Re-crawl; duplicates should canonicalise to one URL.

sources.title: Google: How to specify a canonical URL

rules.title: HTTP version does not redirect to HTTPS
rules.description: The http:// version of the site responds without redirecting to https://, creating duplicate versions. Google prefers HTTPS URLs as canonical.
rules.fix: Redirect all http:// URLs to https:// with 301/308.
rules.verify: Fetch http:// homepage and confirm a permanent redirect to https://.

rules.title: www and non-www both serve content
rules.description: Both the www and non-www host return 200 without redirecting to one preferred host.
rules.fix: Pick one host and 301-redirect the other.
rules.verify: Fetch both hosts and confirm one redirects.
